extracted.intended_audience: Heads of executive departments and establishments; federal agency officials responsible for Privacy Act implementation and system-of-records reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for federal agencies on when and how to prepare and submit Reports on New Systems (or reports on changes to systems) required by the Privacy Act (5 U.S.C. 552a(o)), including required contents, supporting documentation, timing, distribution, and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger — New system proposed
rubrics_metrics.description: A Report on New Systems must be submitted when a system of personal records subject to the Privacy Act is proposed. A new system is one for which no public notice consistent with subsection (e)(4) is currently published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a public notice for any specific system is withdrawn, suspended, cancelled, or terminated and subsequently reinstated, the subject system shall be considered a new system and subject to the new system reporting requirement at such time that it is reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger — Changes to existing systems requiring a new system report (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new system report is required for any change to an existing system which meets any of the specified criteria (see individual change criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum enumerates specific types of changes (population, information types, organization/indexing/retrieval, purposes, equipment) that individually require reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change Criterion — Increase or change in number or types of individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Report required if there is an increase or change in the number or types of individuals on whom records are maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes involving the number (rather than the types) of individuals need only be reported when that change significantly alters the character and purpose of the system (e.g., normal increases due to file growth need not be reported). A change resulting from a change in scope of the population covered (e.g., expanding from part of the workforce to all) must be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change Criterion — Expansion of types or categories of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Report required if the type or categories of information maintained are expanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if an employee payroll file is expanded to include data on education and training, this expansion of types/categories of information must be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change Criterion — Alteration of organization, indexing, or retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: Report required if the manner in which records are organized or indexed/retrieved is altered so as to change the nature or scope of those records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: combining two or more existing systems, splitting an existing system into two or more systems, or centralization/decentralization of responsibilities would require a report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change Criterion — Alteration of purposes for which information is used
rubrics_metrics.description: Report required if the purposes for which the information is used are altered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: files currently used as historical military service records being used to make determinations on eligibility for disability benefits would require a report. A proposal to establish or change 'routine uses' will not require a new system report if such use is compatible with the original purposes (i.e., does not create a new purpose), but any new or changed 'routine use' remains subject to the 30-day prior Federal Register notice requirements (5 U.S.C. 552a(e)(11)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change Criterion — Change in equipment configuration creating greater access risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Report required if the equipment configuration (hardware and/or software) on which the system is operated is changed so as to create the potential for greater or easier access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: addition of a telecommunications capability which could increase the risk of unauthorized access would require a report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Requirement — Narrative statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency report shall include a brief narrative statement, normally not to exceed four pages, which describes the purposes of the system, identifies the authority under which the system is to be maintained, evaluates probable or potential effects on privacy and other rights, and describes steps taken to minimize the risk of unauthorized access including discussion of higher or lower risk alternatives considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A more detailed assessment of risks and specific administrative, technical, procedural, and physical safeguards shall be available on request. The narrative should make reference to supporting documentation rather than restating it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Documentation — Advance copy of new or revised system notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Append an advance copy of the new or revised system notice consistent with 5 U.S.C. 552a(e)(4) which the agency proposes to publish for the new or altered system(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proposed alterations, provide documentation in the same form as the proposed public notice. If superseding the entire existing notice, highlight changes from the currently published notice by underlining new or revised portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Documentation — Advance copy of new or changed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Append an advance copy of any new rules or changes to published rules (consistent with 5 U.S.C. 552a(e)(11) and (f)) which the agency proposes to issue for the new or altered system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no change to existing rules is required for the proposed new or altered system, the report shall so state. Proposed changes to existing rules should be provided in a manner similar to the system notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Documentation — Advance copy of proposed exemption rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Append an advance copy of any proposed rules setting forth the reasons why the system is to be exempted from any specific provision (consistent with 5 U.S.C. 552a(j)) or if the agency head plans to invoke any exemptions for the new or altered system(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the proposed exemption rules in the report when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated Reporting for Multiple Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: When changes to computer installations, communications networks, or other general changes affecting multiple systems of records are made, a single consolidated new system report may be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In consolidated reports, the narrative should address overall privacy implications, identify all systems affected, and briefly describe any unique impacts on any specific system. Supporting documentation shall be provided for each system of records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Inventory Update (planned)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB, in cooperation with the National Archives and Records Service, is developing a perpetual inventory of all systems of records subject to the Act; agencies will be requested to provide a simple report to facilitate maintenance of the Federal inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This portion of the report is not in effect until further instructions are issued; detailed plans are still being developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format — Narrative and supporting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: No standard format has been established for the narrative statement; agencies should present the information requested as concisely as possible. Supporting documentation format should, where applicable, be consistent with the publication requirements established by the Office of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative normally should not exceed four pages. The format for the Federal Inventory is being developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution — Recipients and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Two copies of each new systems report shall be submitted to each of the following: Speaker of the House, President of the Senate, the Privacy Protection Study Commission (during its existence), and the Office of Management and Budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely distribution to all listed recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — Submission deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: A report on a proposed new or altered system of records shall be submitted no later than the earlier of: (1) sixty (60) days before any issuance of data collection forms and/or instructions; or (2) sixty (60) days before any public issuance of a Request for Proposal or an Invitation to Bid for computer and/or communications systems or services intended to support the system of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet the earliest applicable 60-day deadline to allow review prior to data collection or procurement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Date
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this Transmittal Memorandum are effective upon issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should comply with these requirements immediately upon issuance of the memorandum.
